_comment: Baked baseline replay per quiz scenario — the run a guest watches before
being asked to pick an upgrade. mkquiz.py builds the 'watch it running'
link from this file and VERIFIES each bake exists under the served root,
so a re-bake that changes the content hash breaks the build instead of
shipping a dead link nobody clicks until it is on screen.
The bake must be the SAME baseline the options were measured against.
chishow is the fw20 cut, which is what docs/show/quiz/chi-loop-urban.json
was measured on — the newer, properly congested chi-show-fw35 scenario is
not baked and is NOT the baseline behind those numbers, so linking it
here would show one network and score another.
'window' is the stretch worth showing on camera and the rate to show it
at, from docs/show/README.md. Everything else in a 12,000-tick replay is
the network filling or a steady state that has already made its point.

merge-pod.window: ticks 4200-10200 at 8x = 75 s: the shockwave forming at the merge and walking 2 km upstream

bottleneck-town.window: ticks 6300-7200 at 1x = 90 s: one full 86 s cycle at every junction with the queues fully developed

chi-loop-cbd.window: the whole run reads; 7000 ticks is the fidelity-gated cut — at 12000 the saturated grid refuses 7% of demand at injection

chi-kennedy.window: the AM peak builds through the whole run; the measured window is the last 8000 ticks

chi-loop-urban.window: the whole run reads; the expressways in this cut run 59-76 km/h, faster than the real thing
